title: Architecture overview
text: EpiSODIC (Epidemiological Signal Observation, Detection, Identification, Classification) R package: outbreak cluster detection assessment system infectious disease epidemiologists. ingests laboratory-confirmed infections, runs statistical rule-based detectors , reconciles raised signals persistent clusters across repeated runs, gives small board epidemiologists dossier formally assess one - full audit trail outbreak reports clinical colleagues (e.g., clinical microbiologists) infection prevention nurses end. narrative summary system’s design, covering parts matter understanding works day day.

title: Architecture overview
text: package open-source software data site-specific configuration . running instance - real organisation’s database, EPISODIC_CONFIG overrides, provisioned accounts - lives entirely outside package, addressed environment variables (EPISODIC_DB, EPISODIC_CONFIG, EPISODIC_GEO_DATA, …; see README’s “Environment variables” table full list). Nothing specific laboratory, hospital, patient can enter repository, repository never holds .

title: Architecture overview
text: Two entry points, one database: episodic_run_cron() expensive work: ingestion, stream enumeration, detection, reconciliation, inside one transaction, partially failed run leaves partial state retry always safe. episodic_run_app() ever performs cheap reads already-computed results, plus small set insert-write actions (classify, close, mute) gated behind authentication. split keeps interactive app fast regardless expensive detection , keeps every write path auditable.
code: # The cron entry point - typically scheduled, e.g. nightly episodic_run_cron(   db_path = "/path/to/episodic.sqlite",   ingest_source = my_extract_and_transform_function() )  # The interactive entry point - a Shiny app, read-only for anonymous # visitors, write access after signing in episodic_run_app(db_path = "/path/to/episodic.sqlite")

title: Architecture overview
text: Cases mandatory input: one row per confirmed-positive laboratory result, deduplicated internally per patient/pathogen/episode. Everything downstream - streams (unit detector watches), detections (detector raised), clusters (reconciliation turned detections across runs), assessment events, rendered reports - derived stored result explainable database alone: run produced , configuration (hashed snapshotted), raw detections. Positivity metadata, institution activity (patient-days), geographic reference data optional, additive inputs - system runs completely without , using raw counts plain PC breakdown instead normalised trend choropleth.

what: The lattice: streams, not one big feed
title: Detection and reconciliation
text: Every case belongs several streams - ward-level stream, institution-level stream, area, province, whole catchment - watched independently. Streams enumerated automatically data every run, newly appearing pathogen creates streams without configuration step: level strict partition one - ward sits inside exactly one hospital, hospital inside exactly one area, - makes suppression () meaningful.

title: Detection and reconciliation
text: farrington (surveillance::farringtonFlexible()) - standard statistical aberration detector streams enough baseline history, run L1/L2 patient-day population offset one exists, busy month quiet one identical transmission-per-patient-day read signal strength. same_place - rule-based detector needing baseline : n cases organism place within k days. catches long-term care institutions, individually sparse statistical baseline, also runs alongside Farrington hospitals, can fire first fast cluster weekly aggregation produced point test. rare_trigger - curated list organisms (inst/config/default.yaml) single occurrence anywhere signal - certain notifiable exceptionally rare pathogens need second case warrant look. mem (mem package’s Moving Epidemic Method) - organisms flagged mem_applicable (influenza, RSV), answering “epidemic started” rather “counts elevated”, pre-/post-epidemic thresholds derived historical seasons. stream’s history feeds back baseline: period assessor confirmed real epidemic excluded farringtonFlexible() sees subsequent runs stream, last winter’s outbreak silently raise winter’s threshold.

title: Detection and reconciliation
text: Detection alone produces burst raised signals every run - underlying cluster otherwise appear new row every single time still elevated. Reconciliation, run per stream immediately detection inside transaction, turns small number persistent clusters assessor can actually track: Detections different detectors whose intervals overlap merge one candidate episode. candidate matched currently open clusters stream interval overlap (proximity within case_free_days): match creates new cluster; one match extends existing one recomputes score; multiple matches merge, oldest surviving others’ assessment history preserved, never discarded. cluster nobody’s seen new candidate run gets runs_since_detected counter incremented; past threshold, assessment ever recorded, closes automatically expected variation. Anything assessor actually classified worth watching never auto-closed - person closes . anchor sample date, late-arriving case can legitimately change already-detected signal retrospectively - reconciliation deliberately re-runs rolling window, “today”, sized empirical reporting-delay curve.

what: Suppression: one lattice, not five parallel views
title: Detection and reconciliation
text: Without suppression, one real outbreak appear five separate clusters - one per level - burying actual signal restatements . reconciliation: child cluster suppresses parent accounts parent’s excess (rise local; wider view adds nothing). parent suppresses children rise spread across several single dominant one (rise diffuse; five separate area-level clusters just noise). suppressed clusters never discarded - stay attached context, visible surviving cluster’s detail screen.

what: Derived state, not a stored status
title: Detection and reconciliation
text: cluster’s displayed state (new, assessing, monitoring, ready close, closed, needs reassessment) computed, every time, classification history, case-free clock, whether changed since last assessed - never stored hand-edited. See episodic_derive_state() exact rule state_derive.R’s tests every transition covers.

title: Connect your own laboratory data — episodic_ingest_interface
text: episodic_ingest_columns lists required columns, order: source_key unique identifier result, stable across repeated runs (used detect duplicates). patient_key pseudonymised patient identifier, consistent patient across results. sample_date, receipt_date Dates sample taken received laboratory. pathogen pathogen name, exactly laboratory reports (e.g. "Escherichia coli", "Influenza "). Used verbatim - never matched taxonomy - since detection must work pathogen lab can report, viral . isolate may appear one pathogen value epidemiologically useful (e.g. ETEC isolate reported "Escherichia coli" "ETEC", monitored separately). care_line Typically "hospital" "primary_care". institution_key, institution_display_name, institution_type reporting institution's identifier, display name, type. municipality, ward, specialism, pc location clinical context, available. sex, age Patient demographics, available. confirmed-positive results belong feed - outcome column, include negative results . also want denominator (tests performed, positivity rate), supply separately pre-aggregated counts; see R/ingest_denominator.R. ingestion source shipped package synthetic generator (episodic_ingest_source_synthetic()) used bundled demo - useful template base .

text: dashboard available Dutch, English, Spanish, French, German, Mandarin Chinese, Hindi, (Modern Standard) Arabic. user-facing text stored translation keys (e.g. "nav.clusters") rather hardcoded R code, episodic_tr() looks key requested language. key exist language shown [[key]] rather silently left blank, missing translation easy spot.

title: EpiSODIC 0.3.0
text: Expanded dashboard translations Dutch English also cover Spanish, French, German, Mandarin Chinese, Hindi, (Modern Standard) Arabic (inst/i18n/{es,fr,de,zh,hi,ar}.json), covering top spoken languages world alongside Dutch English. Pass lang [episodic_run_app()], [episodic_demo()], [episodic_report_render()]. episodic_format_date_range() now also formats month names languages, sourced inst/i18n/*.json files every piece dashboard text. Added EPISODIC_LANGUAGE environment variable, read [episodic_run_app()], [episodic_demo()], [episodic_report_render()], [episodic_tr()] default lang passed explicitly. Falls back "en" unset.

title: EpiSODIC 0.2.0
text: Rewrote documentation epidemiologist audience: every man page now written someone running configuring EpiSODIC, contributor reading source. Several related functions combined onto single help page (dashboard chart builders, HTML formatting helpers, geographic reference data), examples now show output instead assigning silently. EPISODIC_DB also accepts mysql:// DSN (episodic_db_dsn_mariadb() / episodic_db_dsn_mysql()) run MariaDB/MySQL instead SQLite, schema file. Renamed internal episode_/episode- prefix episodic_/ episodic- throughout (functions, database tables, CSS classes) match package name. Package version shown Shiny app header. README screenshots now ship man/figures/ render CRAN ; removed placeholder pkgdown reference pages trimmed internal dev notes (data-raw/).

title: EpiSODIC 0.1.0
text: First development version. Detection: automatic lattice enumeration, five detectors (farrington, ears, same_place, rare_trigger, mem), cluster reconciliation across runs, cross-lattice suppression, baseline feedback. Interface: bilingual (NL/EN) Shiny app, read-anonymous visitors; dossier view (epi curve, trend, geography, Rt, line list); audit-trailed classification workflow; Performance screen. Reporting: versioned Quarto outbreak reports small-count suppression. SQLite backend; optional EpiEstim/mem/quarto/sf integrations, documented fallback absent. episodic_demo() runs whole system bundled synthetic data - credentials configuration required.
